intervention: Mediterranean diet + extra-virgin olive oil or nuts
notes: Prevención con Dieta Mediterránea. High CV risk, no CVD. MedDiet reduced MACE 30% (HR 0.70, p=0.004). Stroke reduced 39%. LANDMARK nutrition trial. Changed dietary guidelines. Spanish trial. NEJM. (Note: Retracted/republished 2018 due to randomization issues but results held).

Post-MI. High-dose omega-3 reduced LV remodeling (LVEDV index -5.8% vs -0.2%, p=0.004). Improved LV systolic function. Events 12.2% vs 18.0% (p=0.08). High-dose fish oil post-MI beneficial for remodeling.

Statin Residual Risk Reduction with Epanova in High CV Risk Patients. Mixed dyslipidemia + CVD/DM. STOPPED EARLY for futility. Omega-3: NO benefit (HR 0.99, p=0.84). Formulation matters - EPA/DHA vs EPA-only. AstraZeneca.

Reduction of Cardiovascular Events with EPA. Elevated TG (135-499), on statin. EPA reduced MACE 25% (HR 0.75, p<0.001). CV death reduced 20%. BREAKTHROUGH: First omega-3 showing CV benefit in large RCT. FDA approved. Amarin.
Chronic HFrEF (any etiology). Rosuvastatin: NO benefit (29% vs 28%, p=0.59). Statins don't help established HF unless indicated for CAD. Statins for prevention, not for HF treatment itself.
HF with cachexia (unintentional weight loss >5%). Intensive nutrition improved weight (+3.2 kg vs -0.8 kg), muscle mass, QOL. Reduced HF hosp (22.6% vs 35.6%, p=0.01). Cachexia is modifiable.
HFrEF men with low testosterone + muscle wasting. Testosterone improved 6MWD (+24m vs -8m, p=0.001), lean mass, strength. Events 18.4% vs 25% (p=0.12). Addressed frailty/sarcopenia in HF.
